- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > 0.0), model frequently overestimates downward moves — adjust downward bias by 2–5% if true outcome shows mean reversion.
- Model underestimates true volatility in early 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3 in last 5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore sentiment — apply sentiment-weighted correction: forecast = model * (1 - |sentiment| * 0.15)
